source_review.notes: Reviewed the primary Herlihy-Wing paper and current official Python, Java Lock/ReentrantLock, Go memory-model, POSIX mutex, SEI CERT lock-order, and LLVM ThreadSanitizer documentation. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. The executable runner's deliberate exclusion of thread primitives is preserved; runtime-thread claims are not inferred from the bounded state model.

evidence: Checked abstract/concrete state, invariant, mutex, invocation/response/linearization events, concurrent/sequential histories, wait/hold/response time, utilization, guarded state, escape, lock-order graph, snapshot, and poisoning.
Checked data-race freedom, memory visibility, linearizability, exception safety, deadlock/progress/fairness, and performance remain separate properties.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter never treats mutex acquisition or release as a universal method-independent linearization point.

evidence: Recomputed model schedule: four workers each write three keys for twelve writes and sixteen total modeled acquisitions including snapshot, stats, get, and validation snapshot.
Recomputed keys 0 through 11, square-value sum 506, size/write count twelve, and detached-snapshot result.
Checked serialized-service reciprocal statement is explicitly an approximate upper bound under a named service-demand model, not an empirical throughput claim.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No wait, hold, latency, fairness, or throughput number is fabricated.

evidence: Verified mutual exclusion orders complete critical effects; sequential core correctness and invariant restoration yield a legal history respecting nonoverlap real-time order.
Verified release/acquire visibility proof requires the target language primitive's synchronization relation and excludes unlocked aliases/reads.
Verified global increasing multi-object lock order makes the lock-order graph acyclic; structured cleanup alone does not restore a half-mutated representation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Pending invocation treatment and timeout-after-effect ambiguity are explicitly acknowledged.

evidence: Reviewed empty/no-op/failure operations, reads/size/equality/format/validation, live views/iterators/mutable elements, check-then-act, snapshots, serialization, and metrics.
Reviewed nonreentrant/reentrant callback entry, two-wrapper reverse ordering, identical objects, conditions/spurious wakes, timeout/cancellation, close/destruction/copy/fork, and partial mutation.

Reviewed starvation/fairness/priority inversion, convoying, long callbacks/I/O/GC, hostile keys/work/output, tenant diagnostics, authorization revalidation, profiler limitations, and production saturation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Limits cover key/value/state size, callback/critical work, wait/deadline, snapshots/serialization, workers/queues, diagnostics, and profiler/test resources.

evidence: The bounded model rejects overlapping ownership and nonowner release, uses try/finally for every modeled access, completes every worker, checks exact map state/write count, releases ownership, and verifies snapshot isolation.
The chapter specifies guarded-state/ownership, linearization, visibility, failure, escape, composition, condition, lifecycle, and progress evidence invariants.
The verification stack includes sequential invariants, bounded history checking, race detection, schedule/fault stress, lock-order analysis, model checking, and production-shaped measurement.
invariant_checking.notes: The executable is a serialization state model, not a real mutex/thread/memory-model experiment.

evidence: Reviewed abstract API/ownership/complete lock coverage, method-specific linearization, visibility, compound operations, snapshots, callbacks, and element aliases.
Reviewed multi-object deadlock, exception/cancellation/condition correctness, lifecycle/fork/copy/serialization, progress/fairness/priority behavior, and serialized contention.
Reviewed history/race/fault/model/performance evidence, security, alternatives, and all five model answers.
proof_review.notes: The one-lock proof is conditioned on no escape and complete critical operations; future methods require renewed audit.

evidence: Linearizability, visibility, failure, composition, condition, and lifecycle proof sections state their assumptions and distinct conclusions.
Performance/queueing discussion is explicitly model/measurement guidance rather than a correctness theorem.
ThreadSanitizer and final-state tests are explicitly limited and cannot substitute for history/progress proofs.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No fairness, FIFO, deadlock freedom, starvation freedom, bounded latency, or scalability guarantee is generalized across mutex implementations.

evidence: The standard-library-only bounded Python state model passed exact eight-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under Python 3.14.4.
It emits evidence=finite_coarse_lock_serialized_model and reproduces modeled ownership, serialized writes, worker completion, snapshot isolation, and invariant checks.
All eight external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed draft module validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No runtime threads, mutex memory visibility, arbitrary schedule/history, race detector, deadlock/progress/fairness, cancellation/fault, close/fork, or performance experiment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: Builds from sequential specification and ownership to the direct linearizability/visibility proof, then systematically breaks the naive wrapper model through compound calls, escape, callbacks, failures, composition, conditions, lifecycle, progress, measurement, and security.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed private guard ownership, all API surfaces, structured release, strong/basic exception policy, atomic compound APIs, snapshot/serialization staging, callback restrictions, global lock order, monotonic deadlines, close/wakeup, fork/copy, contention metrics, race/history/fault tools, tenant authorization, and migration baselines.

pedagogical_review.notes: Derives the core proof from first principles, separates concurrency properties, uses ten varied failure/design examples and a precisely limited executable model, then supplies five progressive exercises with complete solutions.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Herlihy/Wing, Python, Java, Go, POSIX, SEI, LLVM, concurrency, security, performance, reliability, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither arbitrary wrappers/future methods, real thread/mutex execution, language memory visibility, all concurrent histories, callback/element safety, exception rollback, conditions/cancellation/timeouts, lock-order enforcement, deadlock/starvation/fairness/priority behavior, lifecycle/fork safety, race-detector coverage, production contention/latency/throughput, hostile-input resilience, certification, nor deployment fitness.
